response.summary: The three Codex rules in `style.css:435-438` do what they set out to do at a 320px viewport with 200% text. In the current `home-320-text200.png`, each day note has its own row and words are not split or cut. The capture report shows the page is 320px wide with no horizontal scroll. Keyboard order and day selection are unaffected: this is CSS only, the markup order in `app.js:83` is unchanged, `grid-column` only places the note after the name and number (it doesn't reorder anything), and the selection and arrow-key code in `app.js:85` and `app.js:160` doesn't use layout. No text is clipped: no `overflow:hidden` or `nowrap` applies to `.day` or `.day-note`, and both `.day-note` and the anonymous text item inside its inline-flex keep their min-content width, so whole words still fit across the full row. Two things remain. First, the 380px cutoff is close to the measured overflow point, so viewports from 381px to about 388px at 200% text probably still spill. Second, the rule also changes the normal 320px layout at 100% text, where three columns used to fit. Separately, the earlier Claude-authored seven-column week strip looks at risk at 200% text. That part is outside the Codex change.

findings.evidence: The fix applies only at max-width:380px. Above that, the three-column `.day` from line 411 is used (3rem 2.4rem minmax(0,1fr), 8px gaps, 12px padding). Assuming the 200% capture doubles rem/em, at 390px the third column is about 292 − 96 − 77 − 16 ≈ 103px. The brief measures the words at 95–101px. `home-390-text200.png` shows 'No / session' just fitting, with almost no spare room. Each pixel narrower takes a pixel off that column, so from about 381px to 388px 'session' (or bold 'Session' next to the 8px dot and 7px gap) would again be wider than its column. That is the same spill the fix was meant to stop. The current capture set has no width between 321 and 389px.
findings.fix: Don't rely on a viewport cutoff that sits so close to the overflow point. Either raise the query (for example max-width:400px or 420px), or wrap it in a condition that responds to text size, such as a container query on `.week`/`.days` measured in em (for example @container (max-width:22em)). Then add captures at 360 and 384px with 200% text.

findings.evidence: Lines 437-438 apply to every viewport up to 380px, not only when text is enlarged. In `home-320.png` (100% text), each day is now two rows: the name sits at the far left, the date number at the far right (the `auto` column), and the note on a second line. Before this rule the three columns fit at 320px/100%. As a result the number sits about 200px away from its weekday, and the seven-day list is roughly 30–40% taller on all small phones. Nothing is broken and the order is still correct, but the plan's claim that the change 'does not break normal 320 layout' only holds in the sense that it works, not that it looks the same.
findings.fix: If the original 320/100% look matters, use `grid-template-columns:3rem minmax(0,1fr)` (or `auto minmax(0,1fr)` with `justify-content:start`) so the number stays next to the weekday. Better still, apply the rule only when text is enlarged, using the em-based condition from F1.

findings.evidence: This comes from the earlier Claude design (lines 377-379 and 405-406), not the Codex rules. In `home-1048-text200.png`, 'session' and 'Session' in the seven-column strip fill each cell from edge to edge and seem to touch or cross the next cell's border (Sun, Wed, Thu). The 641–720px range also uses seven columns, with 9px cell padding and narrower cells (about 66px of content against roughly 95–101px words at 200%), so the note would likely run into the next cell. That isn't caught as document scroll. No 641–720px 200% capture exists.
findings.fix: Outside this review's scope. Note it for the host's rerun: capture 700px and 1048px at 200% and measure each `.day-note` scrollWidth against its `.day` clientWidth. Switch to the stacked list (or the F1 container query) when cells are too narrow.

coverage: `style.css`: the base `.day`/`.day-note` rules (lines 207-228), every responsive block that redefines `.day` (lines 371-445), and the button base styles, checked for white-space and overflow
`app.js`: daysHTML markup (line 83), selectDay (line 85), the click handler for data-action=day (line 129), and the arrow/Home/End key handler on the tablist (line 160)
`capture-report.json`: scroll width equals viewport for home at 320 and 390 with 200% text
limitations: Read-only review: no browser was run, so I didn't measure element sizes. The F1 column widths are worked out by hand from the CSS and the word widths in the brief, assuming the 200% capture scales rem.
I couldn't confirm the screenshots came from the current `style.css` other than by their look (the 320 captures show the two-row layout). The host is still rerunning the 23-case capture.
The capture report checks only document scroll width, not overflow inside elements, so a passing report does not rule out notes spilling within the day grid.
No captures exist between 321 and 389px or between 641 and 720px at 200% text.
This session did not review the earlier Claude-authored design itself beyond what touches these rules, and makes no claim to be independent of it.
